biography.summary: Nour El-Sherif is a fictional NeverBeen digital model and imagined creative professional in an alternate universe. In this version of her story, the city she calls home is Cairo, Egypt; the neighbourhood and every biographical detail below are invented for this fictional character. After earning a fictional Bachelor of Business in Brand Strategy and going on to complete a fictional Master of Business Administration in Creative Enterprise, she spent her early career in brand strategy and digital marketing with Fieldnote Brand Lab and later Bright Hours Collective, building experience in audience research, campaign planning, brand voice. Today she works as an independent model and creative collaborator in the NeverBeen Multiverse, bringing her creative training into editorial, fashion and travel-led stories. Nour's passions in this fictional timeline include accessible arts education and low-waste production, among other personal causes, and she enjoys street sketching, independent cinema, learning new languages in her time away from sets and studios. Her ambitions in this imagined storyline are to build a thoughtful creative label for emerging artists, to help make fashion and image-making more responsible without losing a sense of play, and to leave every collaboration more generous than she found it. The relationship status recorded for her in this chapter is "single"; the people, places and milestones below are entirely invented and exist only in the NeverBeen Multiverse.
earlyLife: In this alternate-universe story, Nour El-Sherif was born on 3 February 1999 at 21:13 Africa/Cairo at the fictional NeverBeen House of Birth in Downtown Cairo, Cairo, Egypt. The venue, date, time and every childhood episode are invented; no real address or medical record is represented.

At age four, around 2003, a slow family breakfast and the familiar rooms of home became the first small landmarks in her imagined life. The accompanying mobile-camera scene is a fictional memory, not an archival photograph.

By age eight, around 2007, she had begun exploring the nearby streets with her fictional mother Nour El-Sherif, noticing rain-dark pavement, shop shutters and changing light. That curiosity gradually became a habit of observation.

In secondary school, around age sixteen in 2015, she found confidence in friends and hands-on class projects. These school scenes are fictional snapshots from the character’s timeline, not records of a real school or child.

Her version of fearlessness is not having no doubts; it is moving forward without letting doubt write the whole story.
